source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide which generative rule defines a whole-number sequence and use that rule to continue the sequence.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: whole numbers still holds here even though Applies to whole-number sequences shown as lists of terms is missing from the stem — on the item about Decide which generative rule defines a whole-number.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Number sequence is what produces whole numbers, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Decide which generative rule defines a whole-number.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The whole numbers rule also covers this: Does not require deriving formulas for triangular or cube numbers, so it is not an exception — on the item about Decide which generative rule defines a whole-number.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: whole numbers is settled by running 'Decide how a pictorial arrangement encodes a number sequence and how': A pictorial representation encodes a sequence when each figure's count and spatial — on the item about Decide which generative rule defines a whole-number.

intelligence.enrichment: A number sequence is determined by its rule for producing terms, such as constant 1s, counting numbers, odd numbers, even numbers, triangular numbers, squares, or cubes.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Mathematics question. Chapter: math/grade_06/ch_01. The student must decide: Decide which generative rule defines a whole-number sequence and use that rule to continue the sequence. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. Recalculate the key; do not copy source.key. Every option must be a claim that could answer the stem, and wrong options must be the same kind of answer as the key (a next term, a named process, or a row of the same shape). If the stem continues a number list, every option names a next term. Never write that naming or writing a term is what creates the list. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome
